bugs: app/Jobs/QueueAccountStatements.php:11-33 — one job queues all ~40,000 accounts (80 chunkById pages, each pushed to SQS one at a time) and has no #[Timeout], so it falls back to the worker default (60s) and #[Tries(1)]. If it times out partway through, the rest of the accounts are never queued. The run then finishes as completed_with_errors with failed_accounts=1, which does not match total_accounts.
No cleanup for job_batches or failed_jobs: nothing schedules queue:prune-batches or queue:prune-failed, and every failed account leaves a failed_jobs row. The queue tables grow every month.

total_accounts is counted at start, but accounts are queued later. Accounts deleted mid-run (DeleteWhenMissingModels) count as successes, so total no longer equals the number processed. This is minor.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/QueueAccountStatements.php:28 — the job that queues the whole account set is one long, non-resumable unit and has no timeout set
tests/Feature/StatementRunTest.php:48-53 — calls Bus::fake() for no reason and only checks a constructor property
app/Actions/StartStatementRun.php:23 — onQueue is set on the batch and again in each job constructor
app/Jobs/QueueAccountStatements.php:21 — the comment is useful, but it sits above handle() instead of the batch()->add() call it explains
strengths: Bus::batch with allowFailures plus a finally callback means one failing account does not stop the others, and the run always reaches a final status
FinishStatementRun claims the run with a conditional update (where status = running), so the summary email is sent only once
SendAccountStatement throws when Storage::put returns false, so the owner is emailed only after the file exists (probe confirmed)
StatementReady attaches the PDF with Attachment::fromStorageDisk
Uses modern attributes: #[Tries], #[Timeout], #[DeleteWhenMissingModels], #[Scope], #[Fillable], and an enum cast
Tests run the real database queue through queue:work and cover the single-failure, no-account, inactive-account and file-content cases

bugs: app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:34-39 — ignores the return value of Storage::put. If the write fails (put returns false), StatementReady is still emailed and the job counts as a success. A probe confirmed this. It breaks the requirement to email only after the file exists.
No cleanup for job_batches or failed_jobs: nothing schedules queue:prune-batches or queue:prune-failed, so the queue tables grow every month.
total_accounts is counted at start, but accounts are queued later. Accounts deleted mid-run count as successes. This is minor.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:23 — serialises the whole StatementRun model into each of the ~40k jobs, which adds one query per job when only the id is needed
app/Actions/CompleteStatementRun.php:18-20 — passes ->value explicitly for status even though the model has an enum cast
tests/Feature/StatementRunTest.php:18 — uses the older uses(RefreshDatabase::class) in the file instead of setting it once in Pest.php
tests/Feature/StatementRunTest.php:75 — does not check the queue:work exit code, and most tests run on the sync queue, so the real asynchronous path is only tested once
app/Mail/StatementReady.php — does not attach or link the stored PDF
strengths: DispatchStatementJobs pages through accounts with a keyset query and queues its own follow-up job. Each page is bounded, so queuing 40k accounts cannot run into a timeout.
Has a test that runs more than one page (1001 accounts)
Uses a batch with allowFailures and finally, plus a conditional update so the run completes and the summary is sent only once; a test checks this
Gives the batch a name, which helps when inspecting it
Uses modern attributes throughout and renders mailables with assertSeeInHtml, including an HTML-escaping check

v.rationale: The two designs are almost the same: a dedicated statements queue, Bus::batch with allowFailures and finally, a seed job that queues the per-account jobs, and a conditional update so the run completes only once. Neither prunes job_batches or failed_jobs. impl-2 handles fan-out at the 40k scale better, because each job queues one bounded page and then queues the next. impl-1 queues all 40k accounts from one job with no timeout set. However, impl-2 has a confirmed bug against an explicit requirement: it emails the owner even when the PDF write fails, because it ignores Storage::put's return value. impl-1 guards this case explicitly and attaches the PDF. impl-1's tests also run the real database queue throughout. Its large seed job is a risk at production scale, but it does not break any stated requirement. I rank impl-1 first by a small margin.
